1.explanation:
• TableExpandHeader: the <th> component that should expose an id for row cells to reference. It currently only spreads whatever id the consumer passes; when no id is provided it renders no id at all.  
• TableExpandRow: uses an expandHeader prop (defaulting to 'expand') passed to its inner TableCell, setting headers="expand" on the <td>. Without a corresponding <th id="expand"> this is invalid.  
• DataTable#getExpandHeaderProps: the method that supplies props for the expand header (including id) is not automatically assigning a unique id. Consumers using the default expansion story never get an id on the header.  
• setupGetInstanceId: the utility for generating unique instance IDs is wired up but never used to auto-populate an id on the TableExpandHeader.  
To fix the a11y violation, DataTable#getExpandHeaderProps (or TableExpandHeader itself) must invoke setupGetInstanceId and pass an auto-generated id to the <th> so that every <td headers="…"> reference resolves to a real header element.
1.bug_scenario: On the Expansion variant of the DataTable, every expandable row’s first cell is rendered with a headers="expand" attribute, but there is no matching <th id="expand"> in the table head. The IBM Equal Access checker flags each <td headers="expand"> as invalid because the referenced id does not exist in the document. In short: cells point to a non-existent header ID.

2.explanation: The accessibility violation stems from a mismatch between the “headers” attribute on TableExpandRow’s <td> (driven by its expandHeader prop) and the id on the corresponding <th> in TableExpandHeader. TableExpandHeader needs to accept or generate an id that matches each row cell’s headers attribute. TableExpandRow’s default expandHeader prop (‘expand’) is hard-coded and may not be synchronized with the actual th#id. The DataTable component’s getExpandHeaderProps and getRowProps methods are responsible for producing matching ids for each header–cell pair; they must be updated to generate a unique id (or propagate a user‐supplied id) to both the <th> (via TableExpandHeader) and the <td headers> attribute (via TableExpandRow) so that screen readers can associate them properly.
2.bug_scenario: On expansion‐enabled DataTable examples, each expandable row’s first cell renders as …, but the matching in the table head either isn’t rendered with an id or uses a different id than “expand.” IBM Equal Access flags that the td.headers value does not reference a valid th#id in the document, breaking the required relationship between data cells and header cells for screen readers.
